terms.title: Crop greenness from satellite
terms.text: A satellite greenness score from 0 to 1. Healthy, dense crops score high. Bare soil scores low.

terms.title: Greener or browner than normal
terms.text: How much greener or browner a place is than its own normal for that month. Much browner than normal is our sign of crop stress.

terms.title: The thirst of the weather
terms.text: Water leaving the field: evaporation from the soil plus water used by plants. ET0 is how much water a well-watered grass would use in that weather.

terms.title: Rain minus the weather's thirst
terms.text: Rain minus the weather's thirst. Below zero the land is drying. Above zero there is spare water. In Ireland that often means waterlogged ground.

terms.title: Wetter or drier soil than usual
terms.text: Soil that is wetter or drier than usual for that place and month. Measured by the SMAP satellite in squares of about 9 km.

terms.title: Chance of frost
terms.text: The chance that the air falls to 0 °C or below in the spring months, when young crops are easily hurt.

terms.title: Crop stress
terms.text: A month when crops in an area are clearly less green than normal for that month. The cause can be drought, wet ground, heat or frost.

terms.title: How sure we are
terms.text: The range our models give for a risk. A wide range means we are less sure. Your own knowledge of the field matters most there.

terms.title: Satellite data and ground data
terms.text: Satellites see every field, every week, for more than 20 years, but only roughly and from far away. Ground data, like a soil test or your own records, is exact but local. Using both gives wide cover and better accuracy.
